output: The Helan Mountains, sometimes called a "mountain island in the sky," separate the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and Yellow River Valley from the arid deserts of the Alxa Plateau to the west. Like the rugged ranges of western North America's Great Basin, the Helan Range isolates dense conifer forests and may support endemic communities of plants and animals found nowhere else. The ecoregion has received little scientific attention, but it is home to several rare species, including blue sheep, blue-eared pheasants, and the endemic Helan pika. Commercial logging remains a serious threat, and the habitat loss it causes puts the region's high biological diversity at risk.

As shown in Fig. 15, the alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and sits noticeably higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum carries a pair of strong spines that are straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes downward toward the rear, leaving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole, the anterior and dorsal surfaces form a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. Seen from above, the nodes of both the petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. These rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is largely smooth, though it usually carries 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture continues around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is everywhere finely but strongly reticulate-rugose, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. The color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 contains the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*. PrhI is an ECF sigma factor required for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. The gene is activated by PrhR and then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 contains the PprhJ promoter region. This promoter responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and it is activated by the ECF sigma factor PrhI. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult female tissues, foxl2b expression was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. We also found foxl2b expression in the testis to be very strong, which agrees with previous findings showing foxl2b presence accompanied by the absence of foxl2a in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may be a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]
[Your Title/Department]

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation following the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), and from it obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE matter, while the slope square terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE neglects, and this gave us a uniform model.

We then built a numerical model using the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering over a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the uniform model agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

The FEM model can also be applied to the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

In a previous life, the human soul traveled in the company of some god and perceived truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the outcome of that earlier struggle. This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reaches as widely as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech, and the majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered poorly in another language.

Subject: A Note on Buraq

Dear Friend,

The world once existed as a blend of reality and myth, and the two were only clearly separated with the arrival of modern comparative biology. Even so, science has not done away with the space in between, where a figure like Buraq lives. We seem to need such transitional figures to connect empirical knowledge with spiritual experience.

Her presence in contemporary culture works as a bridge between rationalist classification and the older power of myth. The idea shows up most plainly in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure combining piety and speed, recurs as a patron saint. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Part of what makes Buraq so useful commercially is how flexible she is as an image and a name. She presides over wings and wheels, but she is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal, and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

With appreciation for your curiosity,

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to the wild world of MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and they are found by towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them, so just take the damage they deal.

The most dangerous ones live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic matters. Monsters usually roam aimlessly even if you bump into them, but if you attack or cast a debuff on an enemy, you will aggro it. That means you get its attention and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern of most enemies is to attack by trying to run into you over and over again. Against these persistent attackers, the best strategy is the easiest one: attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place. Sometimes you will need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

For the full details on the complete list of monsters, check out the MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Remember: aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

This ecoregion covers the moist deciduous forests around the montane rainforests in the northern Western Ghats, in Maharashtra and Karnataka in western India. Its history reaches back to Gondwana. During the Cretaceous period, the Deccan Plate broke away from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and eventually rejoined the northern Eurasian continent. Later geological uplift formed the Western Ghats Mountains, which caught the southwestern monsoon rains and created a moisture gradient running from wet conditions on the windward side to drier habitats on the leeward side. Annual rainfall is between 1,500 and 2,000 millimeters, followed by a dry season of 4 to 5 months. The mean annual temperature is 24 to 27°C, although inland maximums can exceed 40°C.

We are writing to share some information about early hearing development. People usually learn spoken language in the first few years of life. A child who cannot hear well may lose both the ability to speak and the ability to understand what others are saying.

Often, a family only realizes a child is severely hearing-impaired (deaf) after communication problems have already strained relationships at home and slowed the child's social development. This is less likely to happen if the child grows up in a Deaf community that uses sign language rather than spoken language (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

For this reason, many developed countries test a newborn's hearing so that a deaf child is not accidentally isolated within a hearing family. Sign language is a complete way to communicate, but literacy still depends on understanding speech, since in most written languages the sound of a word is represented by symbols.

Someone who heard well enough to learn to speak and read will keep that reading ability even if their hearing later deteriorates to the point of not hearing voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak, on the other hand, rarely reads proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence points to early identification of hearing impairment as the deciding factor in whether a child with very insensitive hearing learns spoken language effectively. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

We hope this helps you understand why acting early matters. If you have any questions, please get in touch.

Warm regards,

Transduction is the conversion of physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the basic process by which stimuli are translated into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical inputs are transformed by specialized sensory receptors into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system offers a clear example. Within the retina, rod and cone cells act as the bridge between the physical environment and neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it triggers a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. This molecular shift sets off a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The reduction in this gradient causes a decrease in the electrical signals sent to the brain. More light hitting the photoreceptor therefore results in fewer electrical impulses, and the brain uses this pattern to decode the visual world with precision.

Few insects are better known than the Glow-worm, a curious little creature that carries a lantern at its tail-end. Everyone knows it by name, even if it is rarely seen roaming the grass like a spark fallen from the full moon. The Greeks of old called it the Bright-tailed, and modern science identifies it as *Lampyris*. Fabre's *Book of Insects*, however, is written specifically for children. Its texts come from Alexander Teixeira de Mattos's unabridged translations of the *Entomological Memoirs*, which Mrs. Rodolph Stawell, the author of, among other things, *Fairies I Have Met*, retold for young readers. In doing so she abridged and significantly revised the material, and in places bowdlerized it outright.

Subject: Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It consists of many former industrial cities, among them Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live there, which makes the region considerably larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. There are plenty of motorways, but hitchhiking can still be difficult because the network of minor roads is confusing. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitchhike here, stay on those primary motorways. The smaller roads are extremely hard to work with since hardly any transit traffic uses them. Germany is generally a good country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is the least pleasant part of it for that purpose. Hitching within the Ruhr is comparable to hitching in a big city like Istanbul: the cities are independent, yet to a traveler they feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip.

Best regards,

[Your Name/Company]

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

I hope this message finds you well.

Below are the main findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

The total volume of lung tissue was calculated using the formula: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, which were characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As previously described in reference [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, and lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is expanding the immersive potential of storytelling through electronic games played on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest stage in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that aim to make the player a co-author alongside the original designers, going beyond the role of an avatar in a gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let players pull places from the physical world into their gameworld, and the other way around, which is a first for interactive media. Beyond giving players a role in worldmaking, mobile games abandon linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

The idea of "author-player" worldmaking has existed for some time, and mobile games push the process past the limits of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use the player's sensory experiences of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our experience trying to put that potential into practice through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
